correctness.rationale: For any normalized hyponormal one-fork shift, rank-one child-set blocks show that all square-selfcommutator blocks but the parent-of-fork block are nonnegative. The remaining block is bounded below by diag(X_j^2)-sbb* under sum |b_j|^2/X_j <= 1 and s=sum |b_j|^2. The exact factorization ((2/sigma-x/sigma^2)(x^2+delta)-x)=(1-x)(x-alpha)^2/sigma^2 gives the universal secular bound s sum |b_j|^2/(X_j^2+delta)<=1. This proves the operator lower bound even for countably many rays. An explicit two-level strictly positive construction makes this bound singular, yielding the exact negative eigenvalue -delta. The root-fork case has no potentially negative block. The accompanying checker verifies the exact algebra and 8000 randomized finite reductions; the proof, not the samples, establishes the theorem.

originality.rationale: Pikul (2023) and Pikul (2021) classify when square hyponormality is automatic and construct witnesses to its failure. Jabłoński--Jung--Stochel (2009/2012), Example 5.3.2, already exhibits a one-fork hyponormal shift with a nonhyponormal square. Their identified claims do not calculate the exact universal negative selfcommutator norm over contractive hyponormal shifts, the golden-ratio extremizer, or branch-count independence. Targeted public searches and mathematical research index searches did not identify equivalent or dominating quantitative formulas. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not proof of exhaustive historical priority.

value.rationale: This exact norm-one extremal problem measures the size of the smallest-branching obstruction behind the existing forkless/power-hyponormality classification. It determines a nontrivial algebraic constant and a universal positive-weight optimizer, valid for every stem length and finite/countable branching multiplicity. Such a quantitative bound is not a generic substitution into the qualitative criterion; the sharp affine majorant and two-level equality pattern make the result structurally informative. The same theorem identifies the zero-versus-positive threshold at the position of the only fork.
